stage1_result: Stage 1 found all five level elasticities between 0 and 1, common fixed-effect kappa about 0.25, but weak first-difference coupling.
questions: Is the long-term contraction relation approximately a single sublinear power law, or does contraction accelerate at deep abundance loss?
Does abundance explain effective-component variation after linear time trends are removed, or is the apparent rule mainly a shared long-term trend?
candidate_shape_models_frozen_before_sta: M1: y = k*x through the origin
M2: y = k1*x + k2*x^2 through the origin
model_comparison: Leave one entire population trajectory out; fit on the other four; compute prediction RMSE on the held-out population. Compare mean population-level RMSE, giving each population equal weight.
acceleration_rule: Call acceleration a candidate only if M2 or one frozen hinge has lower equal-weight LOO RMSE than M1 and the fitted late/deep slope is greater than the early slope.
detrended_diagnostic: Within each population separately remove linear calendar-year trends from log(N) and log(E), then estimate the common within-population slope and R2 between the residuals.
interpretation_boundaries: All Stage 2 analyses are post-hoc and cannot alter the frozen Ecology Report.
A better nonlinear shape is descriptive, not evidence of a causal tipping point.
Weak detrended or first-difference coupling would imply a long-term trajectory rule rather than an annual response law.
No named universal exponent will be claimed from five nested population units.
